I will keep my land in the usual winter wheat and summer maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the most steady way for me to use the full year, match the local climate, and reduce the risk of putting all my income on one crop. I already understand this system, the machinery fits it, and the selling channel is clear, so I would not make the year complicated. For wheat, I will aim for a stable yield instead of chasing the absolute maximum. I will use improved seed, apply fertilizer in a balanced way with nitrogen as the main input, irrigate at the key stages, and control weeds, aphids, and disease when needed. After wheat harvest, I will move quickly into summer maize so I do not lose soil moisture or planting time. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because emergence and yield are more reliable for me, keep fertilizer strong enough to support grain filling, and use fewer but timely irrigations and pesticide sprays. On tillage, I will plough or rotary-till ahead of wheat when I need to prepare the field well, but after wheat harvest I will mostly keep maize establishment fast with lighter tillage or no-tillage so I save time and moisture. My goal is not to experiment this year. I will run a familiar, lower-risk wheat-maize system and manage it tightly.
